newsitem.title: USA: IMF's Camdessus - so far, so good on currencies.
newsitem.headline: IMF's Camdessus - so far, so good on currencies.

text.p: International Monetary Fund Managing Director Michel Camdessus said on Monday that the current foreign exchange levels have served the world economy well but there is some question about the outlook, given the expected change in the economic cycle among major countries.
"We have, at this stage, the constellation of exchange rates which has served the world economy well," Camdessus said. "So far, so good."

Camdessus said what was important now was that exchange rates reflect economic fundamentals and follow the strengthening of the recovery of Europe and Japan, which have been depressed. He said that he believed the markets expect that the exchange rate will follow the business cycle.
Camdessus met with reporters after a meeting of the policymaking Interim Committee.

He said there had been some concern expressed among panel members about an increase in the Japanese trade surplus, but he said if exchange rates were to follow the fundamentals, "Trade surpluses in Japan shouldn't normally materialize."

Asked if the launch of European monetary union could lead to disruptions in world currency markets, Camdessus replied, "You could imagine scenarios of that kind." But, he added, "The baseline scenario ... of the (IMF) membership is not this one."

In its communique, the Interim Committee welcomed the progress made toward the establishment of EMU and called the creation of a single European currency a very important international monetary development.
"There is a quite positive perception of what EMU could be," Camdessus said. But he acknowledged that the launch of a single currency could be "very delicate."
